note: Georgia criminal motions catalog. Legal information, not legal advice. 'ocga' and 'court_rules' were confirmed present in the GA.LAW.HELP law database on 2026-11-12 (O.C.G.A. text is the 2022 edition) and are re-checked at answer time; 'unverified_authority' is never shown to users.

motions.name: Motion for bond (bond hearing)
motions.purpose: Asks the judge to set bond so the person can be released while the case is pending.
motions.when_it_applies: May apply when someone is being held and bond hasn't been set or was denied.
motions.how_it_helps: Release lets the person work, keep housing and help prepare the defense.

motions.name: Motion to reduce bond
motions.purpose: Asks the judge to lower a bond that is more than the person can pay.
motions.when_it_applies: May apply when bond was set too high for the person's income or circumstances.
motions.how_it_helps: A reachable bond means release before trial.

motions.name: Motion to modify bond conditions
motions.purpose: Asks the judge to change bond conditions (curfew, ankle monitor, no-contact, travel).
motions.when_it_applies: May apply when bond conditions make it hard to work, care for family, or live at home.
motions.how_it_helps: Workable conditions lower the risk of a violation and re-arrest.

motions.name: Petition for writ of habeas corpus (unlawful pretrial detention)
motions.purpose: Asks a superior court to review whether a person is being held unlawfully, for example with no bond decision.
motions.when_it_applies: May apply when someone is held with no lawful basis or bond is denied without a proper hearing.
motions.how_it_helps: Can lead to release or a proper bond hearing.

motions.name: Request for an appointed lawyer (public defender)
motions.purpose: Asks the court to appoint a public defender for someone who can't afford a lawyer.
motions.when_it_applies: May apply when the person can't afford a lawyer and faces a charge that requires one.
motions.how_it_helps: A lawyer is the single biggest help in finding and filing defenses.

motions.name: Motion to discharge appointed counsel and appoint substitute counsel
motions.purpose: Asks the judge to remove appointed counsel and appoint a different lawyer for good cause, such as a conflict of interest or a complete breakdown in communication.
motions.when_it_applies: May apply when the person already has a public defender or court-appointed lawyer and can show good cause (a conflict, including a co-defendant, or a complete breakdown in communication). The person generally cannot pick a particular appointed lawyer.
motions.how_it_helps: If the court finds good cause, a different lawyer can be appointed. A grievance alone does not remove the lawyer from the case.

motions.name: Motion to suppress evidence
motions.purpose: Asks the judge to throw out evidence from an illegal stop, search or seizure.
motions.when_it_applies: May apply if evidence came from a stop or search done without a valid warrant, consent, or legal reason.
motions.how_it_helps: Without the key evidence, charges are often reduced or dropped.
motions.deadline: Usually within ten days after arraignment unless the judge extends it.

motions.name: Motion to suppress for a false or misleading warrant affidavit (Franks hearing)
motions.purpose: Challenges a search warrant that was based on false statements or left out important facts.
motions.when_it_applies: May apply if the officer's sworn statement for the warrant was untrue or misleading.
motions.how_it_helps: If the warrant falls, the evidence from it can be suppressed.
motions.deadline: Usually within ten days after arraignment unless the judge extends it.

motions.name: Motion for return of property
motions.purpose: Asks the court to return property police seized that isn't contraband or needed as evidence.
motions.when_it_applies: May apply when police took a phone, money, car or other property.
motions.how_it_helps: Gets lawful property back.

motions.name: Motion to suppress statements (Jackson-Denno hearing)
motions.purpose: Asks the judge to hold a hearing and exclude statements to police that weren't voluntary or were taken in violation of Miranda.
motions.when_it_applies: May apply if statements were made after threats or promises, while badly impaired, or after asking for a lawyer.
motions.how_it_helps: Removing a confession or admission can seriously weaken the case.
motions.deadline: With pretrial motions, usually within ten days after arraignment unless extended.

motions.name: Motion to suppress an out-of-court identification
motions.purpose: Challenges a lineup, photo array or show-up that was unfairly suggestive.
motions.when_it_applies: May apply if a witness picked someone out under suggestive conditions.
motions.how_it_helps: A shaky identification can be excluded or attacked at trial.

motions.name: Motion to suppress a breath or blood test (DUI)
motions.purpose: Challenges how a breath, blood or urine test was requested, given or recorded.
motions.when_it_applies: May apply in a DUI case when implied-consent rules, testing procedures or the right to an independent test weren't followed.
motions.how_it_helps: Without the test result, a DUI case can become much weaker.
motions.deadline: Usually within ten days after arraignment unless extended.

motions.name: General demurrer (motion to dismiss a charge that doesn't state a crime)
motions.purpose: Argues the indictment or accusation doesn't charge a crime at all, even if everything in it were true.
motions.when_it_applies: May apply when a required element of the crime is missing from the charging document.
motions.how_it_helps: If granted, that charge is dismissed.
motions.deadline: Within ten days after arraignment unless the judge extends it.

motions.name: Special demurrer (defects in how the charge is written)
motions.purpose: Challenges the form of the charge, such as a vague date, place or description.
motions.when_it_applies: May apply when the charge is too vague to prepare a defense.
motions.how_it_helps: Forces the State to fix or narrow the charge; uncorrected defects can lead to dismissal of that count.
motions.deadline: Before trial (form objections); pretrial motions are usually due within ten days after arraignment.

motions.name: Motion to quash the indictment or accusation
motions.purpose: Asks the court to void a charging document because of a legal defect in how it was brought.
motions.when_it_applies: May apply when the indictment or accusation was obtained or filed improperly.
motions.how_it_helps: A quashed charge must be re-brought; a second quashed indictment on the same charge can bar prosecution.
motions.deadline: Usually within ten days after arraignment unless extended.

motions.name: Plea in bar: statute of limitation
motions.purpose: Asks the court to dismiss a charge brought after the time limit for prosecution ran out.
motions.when_it_applies: May apply when the alleged offense happened long before the charge was filed.
motions.how_it_helps: If the time ran out, the charge must be dismissed.
motions.triggers: statute of limitation|time limit|years (ago|later)|too late to charge|long time ago

motions.name: Plea in bar: double jeopardy / former prosecution
motions.purpose: Asks the court to block a prosecution for the same crime and facts that were already prosecuted.
motions.when_it_applies: May apply when the person was already tried, convicted or acquitted for the same conduct.
motions.how_it_helps: If it applies, the new prosecution ends.

motions.name: Discovery: get the prosecution's evidence
motions.purpose: Formally opts into Georgia criminal discovery so the State must share statements, reports, witness lists and physical evidence.
motions.when_it_applies: Applies in most felony cases once the defense opts in; the defense must share some of its own evidence too.
motions.how_it_helps: Knowing the evidence early shows weaknesses and the best defense.
motions.deadline: The State must disclose no later than ten days before trial unless the court orders otherwise.

motions.name: Motion to compel discovery or for sanctions
motions.purpose: Asks the judge to order the State to turn over evidence it hasn't shared, or to exclude it.
motions.when_it_applies: May apply when the State missed discovery deadlines or is holding back evidence.
motions.how_it_helps: Evidence the State didn't disclose can be excluded or the case delayed in the defense's favor.

motions.name: Brady motion for evidence favorable to the defense
motions.purpose: Asks the court to order the State to disclose evidence that helps the defense or hurts its witnesses' credibility.
motions.when_it_applies: May apply in any case where the State may have favorable evidence (deals with witnesses, inconsistent statements, other suspects).
motions.how_it_helps: Favorable evidence can create reasonable doubt; hiding it can lead to a new trial.

motions.name: Motion to reveal a confidential informant
motions.purpose: Asks the court to require the State to identify an informant who witnessed or took part in the alleged crime.
motions.when_it_applies: May apply when an informant was a key witness or participant, such as a controlled buy.
motions.how_it_helps: Lets the defense test the informant's story and credibility.

motions.name: Motion for independent testing of evidence
motions.purpose: Asks to examine or test physical evidence (drugs, DNA, firearms) with a defense expert.
motions.when_it_applies: May apply when lab results are central to the State's case.
motions.how_it_helps: An independent result can contradict the State's lab.

motions.name: Motion in limine (keep unfair evidence out before trial)
motions.purpose: Asks the judge in advance to exclude unfairly prejudicial evidence, such as unrelated past acts or hearsay.
motions.when_it_applies: May apply when the State may try to use prior acts, character attacks or misleading evidence.
motions.how_it_helps: Keeps the jury focused on the actual charge.

motions.name: Motion to sever (separate trials)
motions.purpose: Asks for a separate trial from co-defendants, or on unrelated counts.
motions.when_it_applies: May apply when a co-defendant's evidence or defense would unfairly hurt the person's own case.
motions.how_it_helps: Avoids guilt by association with co-defendants.

motions.name: Motion for change of venue
motions.purpose: Asks to move the trial to another county because a fair jury can't be found locally.
motions.when_it_applies: May apply when heavy local publicity or bias makes a fair trial unlikely.
motions.how_it_helps: A fairer jury pool.

motions.name: Motion to recuse the judge
motions.purpose: Asks a judge to step aside because of bias or a conflict.
motions.when_it_applies: May apply when the judge has a personal conflict or has shown bias in the case.
motions.how_it_helps: A neutral judge.
motions.deadline: Court rule: within five days after learning of the grounds, with a supporting affidavit.

motions.name: Motion for continuance
motions.purpose: Asks the court for more time before a hearing or trial.
motions.when_it_applies: May apply when the defense needs time to get evidence, a witness or a lawyer.
motions.how_it_helps: Prevents being forced to trial unprepared.

motions.name: Motion for self-defense immunity
motions.purpose: Asks for a pretrial hearing to declare the person immune from prosecution for force used in lawful self-defense or defense of others.
motions.when_it_applies: May apply only if force was used to defend against an unlawful attack.
motions.how_it_helps: If granted, the case ends before trial.

motions.name: Motion for a competency evaluation
motions.purpose: Asks the court to evaluate whether the person can understand the case and help the lawyer.
motions.when_it_applies: May apply when there are signs of serious mental illness or intellectual disability.
motions.how_it_helps: A person who isn't competent can't be tried until competency is restored.

motions.name: Notice of insanity or mental illness defense and evaluation
motions.purpose: Gives notice that the defense will raise insanity or mental illness and asks for an evaluation.
motions.when_it_applies: May apply if, at the time of the offense, the person couldn't tell right from wrong or acted under a delusional compulsion.
motions.how_it_helps: Can lead to a not-guilty-by-reason-of-insanity verdict or a guilty-but-mentally-ill outcome with treatment.
motions.triggers: insan|delusion|psychotic|schizo|mental(ly)? ill|didn'?t know (right from wrong|what (he|she|i) was doing)

motions.name: Motion for funds for a defense expert
motions.purpose: Asks the court to pay for an expert when the person can't afford one and the issue is critical.
motions.when_it_applies: May apply when the case turns on science, mental health or forensic evidence and the person is indigent.
motions.how_it_helps: An expert can rebut the State's expert.

motions.name: Notice of alibi
motions.purpose: Tells the State the defense will show the person was somewhere else, with alibi witnesses.
motions.when_it_applies: May apply when the person was somewhere else when the crime happened.
motions.how_it_helps: Proper notice keeps alibi witnesses from being excluded.
motions.triggers: alibi|wasn'?t (even )?there|somewhere else|out of town|at work (when|at the time)

motions.name: Demand for speedy trial
motions.purpose: Formally demands trial; if the State doesn't try the case within the time the law sets, the law requires acquittal.
motions.when_it_applies: May apply when the defense is ready for trial and the State may not be.
motions.how_it_helps: Can end the case with an acquittal if the State delays.
motions.deadline: File at the court term when the indictment or accusation is filed or the next regular term (later only with court permission).

motions.name: Motion to dismiss for violation of the constitutional speedy-trial right
motions.purpose: Asks the court to dismiss because a long, unjustified delay hurt the defense.
motions.when_it_applies: May apply after a long delay caused mostly by the State that harmed the defense (lost witnesses, faded memories).
motions.how_it_helps: Dismissal of the charges.
unverified_authority: Ga. Const. Art. I, Sec. I, Para. XI

motions.name: Conditional discharge (first drug possession)
motions.purpose: Lets the court defer proceedings for a first drug-possession case and dismiss it after probation.
motions.when_it_applies: May apply to a first drug-possession case with no prior drug conviction.
motions.how_it_helps: No conviction if probation is completed.

motions.name: First Offender treatment
motions.purpose: Lets the judge defer a judgment of guilt; completing the sentence means no conviction.
motions.when_it_applies: May apply if there is no prior felony conviction (some offenses are excluded).
motions.how_it_helps: Avoids a conviction and can keep the record restricted.

motions.name: Request for an accountability court (drug, mental health or veterans court)
motions.purpose: Asks to have the case handled in a treatment-focused court instead of the regular track.
motions.when_it_applies: May apply when substance use, mental illness, or military service is connected to the charge.
motions.how_it_helps: Treatment instead of jail, and charges can be reduced or dismissed on completion in many programs.

motions.name: Request to enter a nolo contendere (no contest) plea
motions.purpose: A plea that accepts a sentence without admitting guilt; the court must agree.
motions.when_it_applies: May apply to non-capital cases when a plea is being considered.
motions.how_it_helps: Can limit some collateral effects compared with a guilty plea.

motions.name: Motion to withdraw guilty plea
motions.purpose: Asks to take back a guilty plea.
motions.when_it_applies: Before sentence is pronounced it can be withdrawn; after, only to correct a manifest injustice (for example, the plea wasn't knowing or voluntary).
motions.how_it_helps: Restores the right to fight the charge.
motions.deadline: Before judgment is pronounced as of right; after that, only on a timely motion showing manifest injustice.

motions.name: Motion for directed verdict of acquittal
motions.purpose: Asks the judge to acquit because the State's evidence can't support a conviction.
motions.when_it_applies: May apply at trial when the evidence, even viewed for the State, demands acquittal.
motions.how_it_helps: Ends the case with an acquittal on that charge.
motions.triggers: directed verdict|not enough evidence|state (has|had) no (evidence|proof)|at trial

motions.name: Motion for mistrial
motions.purpose: Asks the judge to stop the trial because something happened that makes a fair verdict impossible.
motions.when_it_applies: May apply when improper statements or evidence reach the jury and an instruction can't fix it.
motions.how_it_helps: A new trial with a new jury.

motions.name: Request for jury instructions on lesser offenses
motions.purpose: Asks that the jury be allowed to consider a lesser crime.
motions.when_it_applies: May apply when the evidence supports a lesser included offense (for example voluntary manslaughter instead of murder).
motions.how_it_helps: Can mean a much lower sentence.

motions.name: Request for jury charge on justification (self-defense)
motions.purpose: Asks the judge to instruct the jury that justified force is a complete defense.
motions.when_it_applies: May apply at trial when there is evidence of self-defense or defense of others.
motions.how_it_helps: Gives the jury a legal path to acquittal.

motions.name: Motion for new trial
motions.purpose: Asks the trial judge for a new trial because of legal errors, a verdict against the evidence, ineffective counsel or new evidence.
motions.when_it_applies: May apply after a trial with errors or other problems.
motions.how_it_helps: A new trial, and it preserves issues for appeal.
motions.deadline: Within 30 days after entry of the judgment.
motions.triggers: new trial|found guilty|verdict|convicted at trial|lost (at|the) trial

motions.name: Motion in arrest of judgment
motions.purpose: Challenges a judgment for a non-amendable defect that appears on the face of the record, such as an indictment that charges no crime.
motions.when_it_applies: May apply right after judgment when the record itself shows a fatal defect.
motions.how_it_helps: Can void the judgment.
motions.deadline: During the court term in which the judgment was obtained.

motions.name: Motion to modify or reduce sentence
motions.purpose: Asks the sentencing judge to reduce, suspend or probate the sentence.
motions.when_it_applies: May apply after sentencing, if filed in time.
motions.how_it_helps: Less time in custody or on probation.
motions.deadline: Within one year after sentencing, or 120 days after the remittitur following an appeal, whichever is later.

motions.name: Motion to vacate a void (illegal) sentence
motions.purpose: Asks the court to correct a sentence the law doesn't allow, such as one above the legal maximum.
motions.when_it_applies: May apply when the sentence is outside what the law permits for that offense.
motions.how_it_helps: A lawful (often shorter) sentence.
motions.triggers: illegal sentence|void sentence|over the (max|maximum)|more than the (law|max)

motions.name: Motion for jail-time credit
motions.purpose: Makes sure days in custody before sentencing count toward the sentence.
motions.when_it_applies: May apply when pretrial custody days weren't credited.
motions.how_it_helps: Shortens the time left to serve.
motions.triggers: time served|credit for (time|days)|jail credit|days (in jail|locked up) (before|didn'?t count)

motions.name: Request for concurrent sentences
motions.purpose: Asks that sentences on multiple counts or cases run at the same time.
motions.when_it_applies: May apply when there are sentences on more than one count or case.
motions.how_it_helps: Less total time.

motions.name: Notice of appeal
motions.purpose: Starts an appeal to a higher court.
motions.when_it_applies: May apply after a conviction or certain rulings.
motions.how_it_helps: Errors at trial can lead to reversal or a new trial.
motions.deadline: Within 30 days after the judgment, or after the ruling on a timely motion for new trial.

motions.name: Out-of-time appeal (now usually through habeas)
motions.purpose: Seeks an appeal after the deadline passed because the lawyer failed to file one.
motions.when_it_applies: May apply when a requested appeal was never filed. Georgia's Supreme Court has limited trial-court motions for this, so it is usually raised through habeas.
motions.how_it_helps: Restores a lost appeal.
motions.triggers: out[- ]of[- ]time|never filed (my|an|the) appeal|missed the appeal|lawyer didn'?t (file|appeal)

motions.name: Petition for writ of habeas corpus
motions.purpose: Challenges a conviction or sentence for constitutional violations, such as ineffective assistance of counsel.
motions.when_it_applies: May apply after the conviction is final, within the time limits.
motions.how_it_helps: Can vacate the conviction or sentence.
motions.deadline: Generally within four years for a felony and one year for a misdemeanor from when the conviction became final.

motions.name: Extraordinary motion for new trial
motions.purpose: Seeks a new trial based on important evidence found after the regular deadline.
motions.when_it_applies: May apply when material new evidence turns up that couldn't have been found before trial.
motions.how_it_helps: A new trial.

motions.name: Motion for post-conviction DNA testing
motions.purpose: Asks the court to order DNA testing that could show innocence in a serious felony case.
motions.when_it_applies: May apply when DNA testing wasn't done or new methods could change the result.
motions.how_it_helps: DNA evidence can prove innocence.

motions.name: Petition for retroactive First Offender treatment
motions.purpose: Asks the court to apply First Offender status after the fact when the person qualified but wasn't told.
motions.when_it_applies: May apply if the person was eligible for First Offender at sentencing but wasn't informed, and the prosecutor consents.
motions.how_it_helps: Exoneration and discharge without a conviction.
motions.triggers: first offender|wasn'?t told|didn'?t (know|tell me) about first offender|retroactive

motions.name: Record restriction (expungement)
motions.purpose: Restricts access to criminal history records for eligible arrests and convictions.
motions.when_it_applies: May apply to dismissed or dropped charges, some completed sentences and pardoned offenses.
motions.how_it_helps: Fewer barriers to jobs and housing.

motions.name: Request for early termination of probation
motions.purpose: Asks the court to end probation early for good compliance.
motions.when_it_applies: May apply after a period of compliance; long probated sentences are reviewed for early termination.
motions.how_it_helps: Ends supervision sooner.
motions.triggers: early termination|end (my|his|her) probation|get off probation|probation early

motions.name: Defense at a probation revocation hearing
motions.purpose: Contests an alleged probation violation and asks for a lesser sanction.
motions.when_it_applies: May apply when a violation is alleged.
motions.how_it_helps: Avoids or limits revocation time.

motions.name: Parole application support
motions.purpose: Supports a parole request with programs, letters and a release plan.
motions.when_it_applies: May apply when the person is or will soon be eligible for parole.
motions.how_it_helps: Earlier release.

motions.name: Pardon application
motions.purpose: Asks the State Board of Pardons and Paroles for a pardon after the sentence.
motions.when_it_applies: May apply after completing a sentence and a waiting period set by the Board.
motions.how_it_helps: Restores rights and can help with jobs.

motions.name: Medical reprieve / compassionate release request
motions.purpose: Asks the Board of Pardons and Paroles for relief from a sentence because of serious illness or incapacity.
motions.when_it_applies: May apply when someone in custody is seriously ill or incapacitated.
motions.how_it_helps: Release to receive care.

motions.name: Federal habeas corpus petition
motions.purpose: Asks a federal court to review a state conviction for federal constitutional violations.
motions.when_it_applies: May apply after state appeals and state habeas are finished; strict federal deadlines apply.
motions.how_it_helps: Can vacate an unconstitutional conviction.
